name: Anchor

props.description: antd `items`, in document order. Each is `{ key, href, title, target?, children?, replace?, targetOffsetBlockStart? }` — antd's AnchorItem, field for field, with its per-link `targetOffset` on the logical axis. `children` is ONE level of nesting and is dropped (with a warning) when `direction="horizontal"`, as in antd.
props.name: items

props.description: antd `direction`, default `"vertical"`. Horizontal is one scrolling row: the ink rail moves along the block-end edge and nesting is not available.
props.name: direction

props.description: antd `affix`, default `true` — literally antd's own `AffixProps` minus the fields Anchor supplies, which is why Affix is the dependency. `false` leaves the nav in the flow.
props.name: affix

props.description: antd `bounds`, default `5`. Pixel tolerance added to the decision line.
props.name: bounds

props.description: The active `href`, as the controlled triad. `onValueChange` is antd's `onChange` under this library's name, and it reports the link the SCROLL POSITION resolved (antd's own note) rather than what `getCurrentAnchor` substituted. antd's `onChange` is typed `never` and warns.
props.name: value / defaultValue / onValueChange

props.description: antd `getCurrentAnchor` — the last word on the highlight, running INSIDE the resolution with no render round-trip. A controlled `value` outranks it.
props.name: getCurrentAnchor

props.description: antd `offsetTop`, on its LOGICAL axis: where the decision line sits, and the distance `Affix` pins the nav at. Default `0`.
props.name: offsetBlockStart

props.description: antd `targetOffset`, on its LOGICAL axis: where a CLICKED section lands — the room a pinned header needs. Defaults to `offsetBlockStart`, and (as in antd) it moves the decision line too, so a click can never leave the entry it just selected unselected.
props.name: targetOffsetBlockStart

props.description: antd `getContainer`, default `() => window` — the scroll box holding the sections.
props.name: getContainer

props.description: antd `showInkInFixed`, default `false`. Draw the travelling ink even with `affix={false}`; the static rule is always drawn.
props.name: showInkInFixed

props.description: antd `replace`, default `false`. Replace the hash in history rather than pushing it; `items[].replace` overrides it per entry.
props.name: replace

props.description: antd `onClick`, fired before the scroll. A modified click is never hijacked.
props.name: onClick

props.description: Accessible name of the <nav> landmark. antd ships an unnamed <div>; a page routinely carries a breadcrumb, a rail and this, so a localized default ("On this page") applies when omitted.
props.name: label

props.description: NOT props. antd's spellings, kept in the type so arriving from antd's docs is a COMPILE ERROR naming `onValueChange` / `offsetBlockStart` / `targetOffsetBlockStart`, plus a development console.warn.
props.name: onChange / offsetTop / targetOffset

related: Affix — the pin underneath it. antd specifies `Anchor.affix` as `AffixProps`, so the two ship as one stack.
NavList — ROUTE navigation inside a page; its `activeId` is the answer Anchor computes, for a different kind of destination.
LegalDocumentShell — carries its own built-in contents rail for the legal-document case; Anchor is the general one, for content the shell does not own.
Breadcrumb — where you ARE in the hierarchy (`aria-current="page"`), not where you are on the page.
tagline: Ant Design `Anchor` (6.6.5): the in-page section navigation, and the only thing in this library that COMPUTES which section is current. `NavList activeId` takes that answer as a prop. Resolves by antd's rule — the last section whose edge has crossed a single decision line — which is a pure function of scroll position and therefore cannot flicker, suppresses itself during the programmatic scroll a click starts, reads the landing hash before any scroll event, and jumps rather than tweens under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
usage: DO give every target a real `id` and point `href` at it as `#id`. The links are real anchors: middle-clickable, deep-linkable, and correct before JavaScript boots.

DO set `targetOffsetBlockStart` to the height of whatever is pinned above the content, or a clicked section lands under the header. Leave `offsetBlockStart` alone unless the DECISION LINE also needs moving; it follows `targetOffsetBlockStart` by default.
DO use `value` / `onValueChange` when the router owns the current section; use `getCurrentAnchor` only for antd's narrower job of rewriting the resolved link in place.

DON'T reach for NavList for this. NavList is ROUTE navigation — each row is a page the router renders, and its `activeId` is an answer you already have. Anchor's entries are fragments of the page being read, which is also why the current one is `aria-current="location"` and not `"page"`.
DON'T use Tabs either: the sections are all on the page at once and scroll past each other, where a tab panel shows one at a time.
DON'T nest more than one level, and don't nest at all when horizontal — antd allows neither, and this warns rather than rendering a second row the ink rail cannot follow.

DON'T hand-roll the scrollspy with an IntersectionObserver band. A section taller than the band reports nothing, and with several short sections in the band at once the answer depends on scroll direction; both are why this measures against a line instead.
useCases: A long settings or policy page whose sections a reader jumps between, with the current one always visible in the rail.
API or product documentation: the on-this-page rail beside the article, tracking the reader down the page.
A marketing landing page's section nav, pinned under the site header via `affix` and `offsetBlockStart`.
A horizontal section bar on a narrow viewport, where a vertical rail has no column to live in.
